objectives: In modern terms, this course should be named Condensed Matter Physics I. It aims to equip graduate students (or senior undergraduates) with an in-depth understanding of the properties and behaviors of crystalline solids through the use of quantum mechanics and statistical mechanics.
content:
Topics covered: 1. Classical & Quantum Free Electron Gas Model of Metals. 2. Electrons in One-Dimensional Lattices. 3. Crystal Structure. 4. Scattering by Crystals. 5. Electrons in General Periodic Potentials. 6. Dynamics of Bloch Electrons. 7. Lattice Vibrations & Phonons.

Lecture schedule:
Lecture 1: Overview and the Drude theory of metals
Lecture 2: The Sommerfeld theory of metals
Lecture 3: Electrons moving in a 1D lattice - tight binding model
Lecture 4: Electrons moving in a 1D lattice - nearly free electron model and Bloch's theorem
Lecture 5: Lattices and crystal structures
Lecture 6: Reciprocal lattice and Brillouin zone
Lecture 7: Scattering by crystals
Lecture 8: Electrons moving in a periodic potential - general properties
Lecture 9: Electronic band structures I
Lecture 10: Electronic band structures II (including the band structure of graphene)
Lecture 11: Dynamics of Bloch electrons
Lecture 12: Lattice vibrations and phonons I
Lecture 13: Lattice vibrations and phonons II

If time permits: semiconductors, magnetism, topological phases, interacting electrons, superconductivity.

Prerequisites: Graduate Quantum Mechanics I (which may be taken concurrently), or are otherwise comfortable with manipulating Dirac‘s bra-ket notation; familiarity with Graduate Statistical Mechanics I is preferred but not required; knowledge of undergraduate solid state physics is helpful but not essential.

--------------------------------------------
Useful references:

1. Solid State Physics, N. W. Ashcroft and N. D. Mermin, Cengage Learning (1976).

2. The Oxford Solid State Basics, S. H. Simon, Oxford University Press (2013) [pre-published version: http://www-thphys.physics.ox.ac.uk/people/SteveSimon/condmat2012/LectureNotes2012.pdf;
see also the online lectures recording at Oxford: https://podcasts.ox.ac.uk/series/oxford-solid-state-basics].

3. Lectures on Solid State Physics, D. Tong, http://www.damtp.cam.ac.uk/user/tong/solidstate.html

4. Band Theory and Electronic Properties of Solids, J. Singleton, Oxford University Press (2001).

5. Solid State Theory, Volume 1: Basics: Phonons and Electrons in Crystals, G. Czycholl, Springer (2023)  [eBook ISBN: 9783662661345].

6. Fundamentals of Condensed Matter Physics, M. L. Cohen and S. G. Louie, Cambridge University Press (2016).

7. Principles of the Theory of Solids (2nd Edition), J. M. Ziman, Cambridge University Press (1972).

8. Solid State Physics: Principles and Modern Applications (2nd Edition), J. J. Quinn and K.-S. Yi, Springer (2018) [ebook ISBN: 9783319739991]

9. Quantum Mechanics with Applications to Nanotechnology and Information Science, Y. B. Band and Y. Avishai, Academic Press (2013).

10. Introduction to Solid State Physics, C. Kittel, Wiley (2018).
books: Typed lecture notes will be provided, following the main line of presentation in Ashcroft and Mermin—widely regarded as the bible of solid state physics—while the actual lecture material will be drawn primarily from S. Simon’s book and D. Tong’s notes.
